text:
Darcy Kuemper made 41 saves, and Brandt Clarke finished the job in overtime. Clarke's snap shot at 2:43 of the extra period gave LAK a 3-2 win over NYI at UBS Arena, after Matthew Schaefer's third-period goal had erased a two-goal lead built by Artemi Panarin's two first-period goals. The first came on a wrist shot the numbers gave a 4 percent chance of going in.

NYI had the better of much of the night. They put 43 shots on goal to LAK's 27, took 74 shot attempts to 61, and won 34 of 54 faceoffs. Kuemper's work is the reason it didn't show on the scoreboard. NYI's chances added up to 3.41 expected goals (a measure of shot quality, where each chance is valued by how often it scores), and Kuemper allowed two, saving about 1.4 goals more than the shots he faced deserved. Schaefer played 29:24 and took nine shots on goal, and Victor Eklund scored on a power play in the second period. Even so, LAK held the edge in the third (1.24 expected goals to 0.44) and created the best chance of overtime, a 27 percent look for Adrian Kempe that Semyon Varlamov stopped. By the "deserved to win" measure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, LAK came out at 58 percent.

The win goes to LAK, and Panarin was named first star with Kuemper second. NYI leave with a point-less night despite outshooting their opponent, and Varlamov, who stopped 24 of 27, was better than his numbers suggest, though the shot quality was heavily in LAK's favor. The facts here carry no streaks or records for either side.
